title: Map Sum Pairs
statement: Build a map from string keys to integer values supporting two operations. Insert stores a key and value, REPLACING any value already stored under that key. Sum returns the total of the values of every key starting with the given prefix.
constraints: keys and prefixes are lowercase letters, 1 to 50 characters
inserting an existing key overwrites rather than adds
hints: A plain dictionary makes Insert trivial and turns Sum into a scan of every key. A trie makes Sum a walk down the prefix. Both are acceptable at this size; the trie is the point of the exercise.
Store a running total on every trie node, so Sum is just a descent to the prefix node and a single read.

Overwriting is the trap. If a key already exists you must apply the DIFFERENCE between the new and old values along its path, not the new value - otherwise a re-insert inflates every total above it. Keep a separate dictionary of current values to compute that delta.

cases.name: re-inserting a key replaces its value
several keys under one prefix, then an overwrite
